Convert the prices of indices to one currency

Source: R/fct_currency.R
convert_prices.Rd

Each price, in the money of the shares of its index, is multiplied by the rate of its day, the units of the new currency that a unit of that money buys, worked out through the US dollar from the rates of Yahoo Finance (see currency_rates()): a price in yen, for example, becomes price × (euros per dollar) / (yen per dollar) euros. A day without a rate of its own takes the last rate of the week before it; the days without one, as before the rates start, between 1996 and 2006 depending on the currency, are left out. The volume, the VIX, which is not in the money of any shares, and the indices already in the currency are left as they are. The daily rates are not taken at the close of each exchange, so the change of a single day mixes in a few hours of the moves of the currency; over weeks and months this matters little.

Usage

convert_prices(
  history,
  to = c("local", "USD", "EUR"),
  indices = get_indices(),
  rates = NULL
)

Arguments

history

Price history from get_history().

to

"local" to leave every index in the money of its shares, "USD" for US dollars or "EUR" for euros.

indices

Data frame of indices from get_indices(), for the currency of each.

rates

Exchange rates from currency_rates(), downloaded when NULL.

Value

history, with open, high, low and close in the currency, without the days that have no rate.

Examples

history <- data.frame(
  label = "Nikkei 225", timestamp = as.Date(c("2024-01-04", "2024-01-05")),
  open = 33000, high = 33500, low = 32800, close = c(33288, 33377), volume = 0
)
rates <- data.frame(
  currency = c("JPY", "JPY", "EUR", "EUR"),
  timestamp = as.Date(c("2024-01-04", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-04", "2024-01-05")),
  per_usd = c(144.6, 144.6, 0.913, 0.915)
)
convert_prices(history, "USD", rates = rates)
#>        label  timestamp     open     high      low    close volume
#> 1 Nikkei 225 2024-01-04 228.2158 231.6736 226.8326 230.2075      0
#> 2 Nikkei 225 2024-01-05 228.2158 231.6736 226.8326 230.8230      0
convert_prices(history, "EUR", rates = rates)
#>        label  timestamp     open     high      low    close volume
#> 1 Nikkei 225 2024-01-04 208.3610 211.5180 207.0982 210.1794      0
#> 2 Nikkei 225 2024-01-05 208.8174 211.9813 207.5519 211.2030      0
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# the S&P 500 and the DAX in euros, each starting at 100
euros <- convert_prices(get_history(c("S&P 500", "DAX")), "EUR")
plot_compare(normalize_prices(euros), currency = "EUR")
} # }
